Encumber

/en-KUM-ber/ - rhymes with lumber · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Encumber means to weigh down or burden.

Decades of borrowing encumbered the railway with debts that no fare increase could outrun.

Worked Example

The costume shop's prize peacock gown encumbers whoever wears it: a wired ten-foot tail, forty pounds of sequined skirt, and wings that snag on every doorframe, so the actress needs two dressers just to reach the stage.

Encumber is heavier than 'carry': whatever encumbers you actively gets in your way — a load, a debt, a duty. Lawyers even speak of an encumbered estate, property so tied up in claims that its owner cannot freely sell it.

How Encumber Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

burden

burden: the everyday word for loading someone down — encumber stresses how the load hobbles you

saddle

saddle: to dump a duty or debt on someone, as in 'saddled with the paperwork'

Antonyms

unburden

unburden: to lift the load off — shoulders or conscience alike

relieve

relieve: to take away what was weighing or worrying

How Strong Is It? — inconvenience → encumber → immobilize

inconvenience vs. encumber

inconvenience vs. encumber: An inconvenience is a pebble in the shoe — mildly bothersome; it stops far short of encumber.

immobilize vs. encumber

immobilize vs. encumber: Immobilize goes further than encumber — an encumbered mover still inches forward; an immobilized one cannot move at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of encumber.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — en-

Prefix — en-: in, into; cause to be

Root — cumber

Root — cumber: a blockage, a hindrance - Old French combre, a barrier across a river

Put it together

Put it together: En- (put into) + combre (a river barrier) = to drop someone into the logjam. Old French combre was the timber dam that stopped a river, and encombrer meant to block and clog. A true 'cause to' word: what encumbers you turns your errand into a dammed stream.

Use the root in a new word: cumbersome

Use the root in a new word: cumbersome: The donated telescope was so cumbersome that it took four volunteers and a furniture dolly to move it upstairs.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Encumber when the load — physical, legal, or financial — actively hampers movement or freedom: encumbered by gear, by debt, by regulations. Burden is the plainer, more emotional cousin; weigh down is the everyday phrasing. Only encumber carries the lawyer's sense of property tied up in claims.
